document_check.note: Berres, Monsch and Spiegel 2021, Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 13:97, 'Using historical data to facilitate clinical prevention trials in Alzheimer disease? An analysis of longitudinal MCI (mild cognitive impairment) data sets'. It compares five MCI datasets (ADNI, NACC, InDDEx, CNG, BS-MC) that had differing criteria, similar baseline scores and markedly different progression. This matches the cited statement.

cited_result: Five MCI samples recruited under differing inclusion criteria had similar baseline MMSE but differed markedly in later verbal-fluency change and in progression to dementia. Kaplan-Meier transition at 3 years ran from 5.9% (InDDEx) to 46.4% (NACC); at 4 years it was about 10% in the drug trial against over 30% in the other samples.
tool_reason: The cited result compares descriptive incidence (progression to dementia) and change estimates across five MCI samples. It is neither a model nor a causal exposure effect, so the incidence-estimate checklist fits best.

domains.domain: JBI item 1: Sample frame appropriate to address the target population
domains.rationale: The question is how MCI samples from different sources behave, and the five named sources are the objects of comparison.

signalling.question: Was the sample frame appropriate to address the target population?
signalling.quote: We compared data from two North American cohort studies (n=395 and 4328, respectively), one company-sponsored international clinical drug trial (n=831) and two convenience patient samples, one from Germany (n=726), and one from Switzerland (n=1558).

domains.rationale: The datasets were taken as available, with age and education restrictions and exclusions for missing data. Only BS-MC is described as consecutive, and most datasets contain patients outside their own criteria. The rivastigmine arm of InDDEx was included as untreated.

signalling.question: Were study participants sampled in an appropriate way?
signalling.quote: It should also be mentioned that almost all datasets contain patients who did not fulfill one or more of their own study's inclusion and/or exclusion criteria (see comments to Table 3).

signalling.question: Was the sample size adequate?
signalling.quote: ADNI n = 395 NACC n = 4328 InDDEx n = 831 CNG n = 726 BS-MC n = 1558

domains.domain: JBI item 4: Subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: Eligibility criteria per dataset (Table 1), demographics and baseline scores (Table 3) are reported.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: Patients in ADNI and NACC were oldest (74.2±7.5 and 74.4±7.9), those in InDDEx and BS-MC were younger (70.1±7.6 and 69.7±9.1), and CNG (68.0±7.9) comprised the youngest sample.

domains.domain: JBI item 5: Sufficient coverage of the identified sample
domains.rationale: Three-year attrition ranged from 25% to 98% and differed greatly between the samples being compared.

signalling.question: Was the data analysis conducted with sufficient coverage of the identified sample?
signalling.quote: In the five studies considered, the rate of drop-outs after 3 years was quite different: 70% in NACC, 37% in ADNI, 25% in InDDEx, 77% in CNG, and 98% in BS-MC.

domains.domain: JBI item 6: Valid methods for identification of the condition
domains.rationale: Progression was a clinician's overall judgement at each visit. The dementia criteria used in each dataset are not stated, and their similarity across datasets is inferred, not shown.

signalling.question: Were valid methods used for the identification of the condition (progression to dementia)?
signalling.quote: In the five datasets considered, an overall judgement was provided at each patient visit by an experienced clinician as to whether the patient had progressed from MCI to dementia.

domains.domain: JBI item 7: Condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants
domains.rationale: Visit schedules, test batteries, test versions and time limits differed between samples, and some transitions were ascertained at extra visits. These measurement differences can themselves produce between-sample differences in progression.

signalling.question: Was the condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants?
signalling.quote: Time to transition from MCI to dementia was usually ascertained at scheduled visits. Sometimes, however, patients were examined in an extra visit and then classified as being demented.

domains.rationale: Kaplan-Meier curves, per-study Cox models and meta-analyses of change are reasonable descriptive tools. However, interval censoring is ignored and censoring is assumed non-informative despite very differential drop-out. Change scores use available cases only, and the between-sample comparison is not adjusted for baseline differences.

signalling.question: Was there appropriate statistical analysis?
signalling.quote: Transitions to dementia were in most studies ascertained at more or less strictly scheduled visits. We nevertheless applied Kaplan-Maier and Cox Regression analysis assuming continuous time.

domains.domain: JBI item 9: Response rate adequate or managed
domains.rationale: Attrition was high and differential. It was addressed only by argument, with no analytic handling such as sensitivity analysis or weighting.

signalling.question: Was the response rate adequate, and if not, was the low response rate managed appropriately?
signalling.quote: This factor may cause bias and could make studies less comparable.

applicability.rationale: The datasets were downloaded 2012 to 2016 and use older MCI criteria. Half of InDDEx received rivastigmine but was treated as untreated: 'We therefore considered all patients as untreated and included them in our analysis.' (page 3).

overall: High (JBI prevalence checklist: items 5, 7 and 9 No; items 2, 6 and 8 Unclear)
overall_rationale: Under this review's JBI rule, a No on standard and reliable measurement of the condition (item 7) gives high. Here, ascertainment of progression and the test batteries differed across the very samples being compared, and differential attrition of 25% to 98% was not handled analytically.
